risks.note: The statutory auditor qualified the standalone opinion because the Company did not perform impairment testing of Property, Plant and Equipment, investments and other financial assets despite the presence of impairment indicators; the auditor states the Company 'has recognized impairment loss in respect of fixed assets amounting to Rs.58,748.44 lakhs' but that 'the impairment assessment has not been supported by adequate documentation and appropriate determination of recoverable amount as required under Ind AS 36'.
risks.risk: Qualified audit opinion - impairment testing not performed under Ind AS 36

risks.note: In the absence of sufficient and appropriate audit evidence on the assumptions used in estimating future cash flows and discount rates, and in the absence of an impairment assessment or external valuation, the auditor says it is unable to determine whether any adjustment is necessary to the carrying value of PPE, investments and other financial assets - so reported asset values may not be reliable.
risks.risk: Carrying value of assets not auditable

risks.note: The Basis for Qualified Opinion carries a second head, 'Implementation of status of the Resolution plan', noting the Company was admitted into corporate insolvency, and the auditor adds an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to Note 1 of the financial statements. Execution of the NCLT-approved plan under new management is therefore not yet a closed item.
risks.risk: Insolvency / Resolution Plan implementation still an open audit matter

risks.note: MD&A: 'The weak-link of your company historically has been the Marketing and Revenue generation despite the fact that the company has cutting-edge business and better than contemporary products. This gap needs to be bridged forthwith as the top most priority.' Revenue is very small relative to the cost base, so the demand-side gap is the core going-concern issue.
risks.risk: Marketing and revenue generation is the acknowledged structural weak link

risks.note: MD&A states the Company operates in a single segment, India's Power Transmission and Telecom Infrastructure space, with no product, customer or geographic diversification disclosed - leaving earnings exposed to one end-market and one country.

The Board's Report describes a steel business pivoting to steel-as-a-service plus a venture studio investing in startups, while the MD&A describes a single segment in power transmission and telecom infrastructure. The two stated identities are not reconciled anywhere in the report, and the venture studio is an unproven model with no disclosed capital plan, timeline or team.

MD&A flags that HR management 'needs to be strengthened in a large measure' to manage discipline, compensation, reward/redressal schemes and career progression - a capability gap for a company attempting a turnaround and a new venture-investing business.
risks.risk: Human resources management discipline needs strengthening

risks.note: Corporate Information records a new Chairman & Non-Executive Director appointed w.e.f. 21 Nov 2025, a Wholetime Director resigned w.e.f. 07 Nov 2025 and an Independent Woman Director resigned w.e.f. 03 Jan 2026 - substantial board turnover in the same year control changed under the Resolution Plan.
risks.risk: Board and management churn during the turnaround

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
